questions.q: In the Tasty Bytes example, which role creates tb_test_role, and which role grants it privileges?
options: SECURITYADMIN creates it; USERADMIN grants privileges
USERADMIN creates it; SECURITYADMIN grants privileges
ACCOUNTADMIN does both
SYSADMIN creates it; PUBLIC grants privileges
questions.explain: USERADMIN creates the role with CREATE OR REPLACE ROLE; SECURITYADMIN then grants it warehouse, database, and table privileges — a deliberate separation of duties.

questions.q: What does a role have access to immediately after CREATE ROLE, before any GRANT statements run against it?
options: Everything SYSADMIN has
Nothing — zero privileges, per Snowflake's least-privilege-by-default model
Whatever the creating user already had access to
Read-only access to all databases in the account
questions.explain: A freshly created role starts with no access to anything. The object browser screenshots show this directly: an empty browser until privileges are explicitly granted.

questions.q: Why is GRANT ROLE tb_test_role TO USER identifier($my_user_var) a necessary step, separate from the privilege grants?
options: It isn't necessary — privilege grants alone let anyone use the role
Creating a role and granting it privileges doesn't let any user actually use that role; a separate GRANT ROLE ... TO USER is required
It deletes the role after use
It only works for the ACCOUNTADMIN role
questions.explain: A role can have all the privileges in the world, but until it's granted to a user, nobody can switch into it and use it — this is the step that's easy to forget.

questions.q: What visibly changes in the Snowsight object browser after GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE ... TO ROLE runs?
options: Nothing changes until the user logs out and back in
The database becomes visible in the object browser for that role, immediately
The database is deleted
The role's name changes
questions.explain: The before/after screenshots show exactly this: an empty object browser, then the granted databases appearing immediately after GRANT USAGE runs — no refresh or re-login needed.

questions.q: What is a 'functional role' as described in this lesson, in contrast to a system-defined role?
options: A role that can only be used for SELECT statements
A custom role (like tb_test_role) built for a specific job, as opposed to one of the six built-in roles like SYSADMIN or SECURITYADMIN
A role that has no privileges and never will
A synonym for ACCOUNTADMIN
questions.explain: Functional roles are custom-built for specific jobs (like tb_test_role here), typically granted underneath SYSADMIN, distinct from the six system-defined roles covered in Lesson 3.
